findings.description: The RDS instance sets storage_encrypted = false, so the database storage, automated backups and read replicas are written unencrypted. Combined with the publicly reachable endpoint, any compromise of the underlying storage or a snapshot exposes the data in cleartext.

publicly_accessible = true gives the RDS instance an internet-routable address. The MySQL endpoint is exposed outside the VPC boundary, materially expanding the attack surface for an unencrypted database whose master username is the guessable 'admin'.

The policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*", i.e. full control of S3, EC2 and RDS across the whole account. Any compromise of the EC2 instance that assumes catalog_app_role yields account-wide privilege escalation and the ability to read/modify/delete all data and security controls.

The user_data startup script writes the plaintext database password (var.password) and DB username into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. This secret is embedded in the instance user data (readable via the EC2 metadata service by any process on the host) and is persisted in cleartext on the instance's disk, exposing credentials to anyone with host or metadata access.

The database security group allows egress to 0.0.0.0/0 on all ports and protocols, so a compromised database instance can freely reach the internet and exfiltrate data. Legitimate database egress should be restricted to required destinations.
